data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient than a decentralized network because the 'complexity cost' of managing diverse, independent services introduces higher rates of human operational error and slower security patching.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The internal redundancy of the large service is managed by a coordination layer (e.g., Paxos/Raft) whose own complexity becomes the primary source of correlated failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure mode is a logic bug in the core application code that is replicated across all redundant nodes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized networks suffer from 'patch latency' where a critical vulnerability remains open in a subset of nodes long after it is fixed elsewhere. Conversely, a large service can deploy a global fix instantly. The lack of centralized coordination in a decentralized network leads to fragmented security postures, where the 'weakest link' can be exploited to cascade failure through the network via interdependent API calls.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
